body:
Thanks for the contribution. I reviewed this change closely.

child.name is already a byte slice. Passing it directly to zip already uses IntoIterator for a byte-slice reference, which produces the same slice iterator as child.name.iter(). As a result, this change is behaviorally equivalent and does not improve safety, type consistency, or performance. The added comment also implies that the previous safe Rust expression was less robust, which is not the case.

The PR title mentions test cleanup, but no tests were changed. The existing ginux-command unit tests pass, though they do not demonstrate any benefit from this change.

Could you point to a concrete compiler error, failing case, or measurable improvement that this addresses? Without that evidence, I do not see a reason to merge this change.
